chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdillah ibn Jabalah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever deliberately leaves throwing the pebbles at the Jamarat, women do not become permissible to him, and he must perform Hajj again next year."

And the order (of throwing) is obligatory in the throwing; it is required that he begin with the Jamarat al-Uzma, then the middle one, then Jamarat al-Aqabah. Whenever he deviates from any of them or throws them upside down (out of order), it is obligatory upon him to repeat (the throwing). He narrated.

key_terms.لَمْ تَحِلَّ لَهُ النِّسَاءُ: Women do not become permissible to him

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for deliberately skipping the stoning of the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that deliberate omission of the Jamarat stoning invalidates the 'tahlil' (permissibility) of marital relations, necessitating a repeat of Hajj the following year, a ruling derived from the principle that Jamarat is a fundamental pillar (rukn) of Hajj. The hadith further emphasizes the obligatory nature of the specific sequence (Jamrah al-Ula, al-Wusta, then Jamrah al-Aqaba), where any deviation or inversion requires the pilgrim to repeat the stoning ritual entirely.
